_comment: Department of Basic Education Grade 10 Physical Sciences P2 (Chemistry), November 2019 national common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The guideline is
bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. memo_answer gives the guideline's
working and final answers (tick marks removed); diagrams, graphs and circuits are described in
brackets in the question text. Data sheets printed with the paper are not transcribed.
Both PDFs were obtained from the Eastern Cape Department of Education exam archive (source_url); the
page headers read 'DBE/November 2019' and 'CAPS - Grade 10', i.e. this is the national DBE paper
FORMAT: 150 marks, 2 hours, eight compulsory questions (Q1 multiple choice 20 marks).
copyright: © Eastern Cape Department of Education, 2019. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.
subject: Physical Sciences

questions.context: QUESTION 1: MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTIONS. Various options are provided as possible answers to the following questions. Choose the answer and write only the letter (A-D) next to the question numbers (1.1 to 1.10) in the ANSWER BOOK, e.g. 1.11 E. Each question has only ONE correct answer.
questions.text: Nitrogen gas is an example of a/an … A element. B compound. C heterogeneous mixture. D homogeneous mixture.

The heating curve, not drawn to scale, of a compound is shown below. [Graph of temperature (°C) against time (s): horizontal section AB at 40 °C, rising section BC from 40 °C to 300 °C, horizontal section CD at 300 °C.] During which section(s) on the curve will the potential energy of the compound INCREASE? A BC only B CD only C AB and CD D AB, BC and CD

The unbalanced equation for a chemical reaction is shown below: CH4 + O2 → CO2 + H2O. Which ONE of the following represents the coefficients of reactants and products in the BALANCED equation? (CH4 | O2 | CO2 | H2O) A 2 | 1 | 2 | 1; B 1 | 1 | 2 | 2; C 1 | 2 | 1 | 2; D 2 | 2 | 1 | 1

Consider the Aufbau diagram of an element below. [Aufbau diagram: 1s ↑↓; 2s ↑↓; 2p ↑↓ ↑↓ ↑↓; 3s ↑↓.] The element is a/an ... A halogen. B noble gas. C alkali metal. D alkaline-earth metal.

questions.text: Which ONE of the following equations represents a precipitation reaction? A NaOH + HCℓ → NaCℓ + H2O B NaCℓ + HNO3 → NaNO3 + HCℓ C NaCℓ + AgNO3 → AgCℓ + NaNO3 D Na2CO3 + 2HCℓ → 2NaCℓ + CO2 + H2O
The air surrounding the Earth is the … A biosphere. B lithosphere. C atmosphere. D hydrosphere.

questions.context: QUESTION 2 (Start on a new page.) Most elements found on Earth are metals. All metals have a metallic structure. 2.1 For a metallic structure, write down the:
questions.text: Type of particles present
Type of chemical bond formed between particles
In which region on the periodic table are metals found? Choose from LEFT or RIGHT.
Write down the SYMBOL of a metal which is a liquid at room temperature.

questions.context: 2.4 To prevent iron from rusting it is often mixed with other metals, e.g. stainless steel is a mixture of iron, chromium and nickel.
questions.text: Is stainless steel a HOMOGENEOUS or HETEROGENEOUS mixture? Give a reason for the answer.
questions.memo_answer:
Homogeneous
Uniform composition / separate particles cannot be distinguished / all components are in the same phase.

questions.text: Rusting is the formation of iron(III) oxide. Write down the FORMULA of iron(III) oxide.
questions.topic: Representing chemical change: formulae and equations

questions.context: 2.5 The physical properties of two substances, A and B, are shown in the table below. [SUBSTANCE | DENSITY (g·cm⁻³) | ELECTRICAL CONDUCTIVITY | THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY: A | 4,94 | Poor | Poor; B | 7,87 | Good | Good]
questions.text: Which ONE of the substances, A or B, has the smaller mass to volume ratio? Give a reason for the answer.
Explain the difference between electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity.
questions.memo_answer: Electrical conductivity is the conduction of electric current/charge and thermal conductivity is the conduction of heat.

questions.text: Which ONE of the substances, A or B, is a metal? Give a reason for the answer.
questions.memo_answer:
B
B has a high density / B is a good conductor of electricity / B is a good conductor of heat.

questions.context: QUESTION 3 (Start on a new page.) 3.1 The three isotopes of magnesium are Mg-24, Mg-25 and Mg-26. The percentage abundance of the three isotopes is 80%, 10% and 10% respectively.
questions.text: Define the term isotope.
questions.topic: The atom: structure, isotopes and electron configuration
questions.memo_answer:
Atoms of the same element having the same number of protons, but different numbers of neutrons.
OR Same atomic number, but different mass numbers.

questions.context: QUESTION 4 (Start on a new page.) A section of the periodic table is shown below. Imaginary symbols are used to represent some of the elements. [Period 1: L in group 18. questions.context: 4.2 The first ionisation energy of element A is 400 kJ·mol-1.
questions.text: Define the term first ionisation energy.
questions.memo_answer: First ionisation energy is the energy needed per mole to remove the first electron from an atom in the gaseous phase.

questions.text: The first ionisation energy of element A can be represented by the following incomplete equation: A(g) + 400 kJ·mol⁻¹ → ... + ... Copy the equation above into the ANSWER BOOK and complete it.
Atoms of element J release the most energy when gaining electrons to form negative ions. Write down ONE word or term for the underlined phrase.

questions.context: (Start on a new page.) Consider the compound Aℓ2(SO4)3.
questions.text: Write down the NAME of the compound above.
questions.topic: Representing chemical change: formulae and equations

questions.text: Define the term molar mass.
questions.memo_answer: The mass of one mole of a substance measured in g·mol⁻¹.

questions.context: 5.3 Calculate the following for Aℓ2(SO4)3:
questions.text: Its molar mass
questions.memo_answer:
M(Aℓ2(SO4)3) = 2(27) + 3(32) + 12(16) = 342 g·mol⁻¹
NOTE: if the unit is omitted, max. ½.

questions.text: Its percentage composition
questions.topic: Quantitative aspects: concentration and empirical formula

questions.text: The number of moles present in 85,5 g
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 5.3.1.)
n(Aℓ2(SO4)3) = m / M = 85,5 / 342 = 0,25 mol

questions.text: The number of aluminium atoms present in 85,5 g
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 5.3.3.)
Number of Aℓ atoms = n x NA x number of atoms = (0,25)(6,02 x 10²³)(2) = 3,01 x 10²³ atoms

questions.context: 5.4 Particles of Aℓ2(SO4)3 are bonded in a crystal lattice. Write down the following for this crystal lattice:
questions.text: The name
The particles of which it consists
questions.memo_answer:
Aℓ³⁺ / aluminium ions / positive ions
SO4²⁻ / sulphate ions / negative ions

questions.text: TWO physical properties
questions.memo_answer: Any TWO: brittle; hard; non-conductor of electricity; non-conductor of heat; high melting point.

questions.memo_answer: The number of moles of solute per cubic decimetre/litre of solution.

questions.text: Calculate the concentration of the solution.

questions.context: QUESTION 6 (Start on a new page.) 6.1 The first step in the extraction of zinc from zinc sulphide (ZnS) is the combustion of ZnS in oxygen. The balanced equation for the reaction is: 2ZnS(s) + 3O2(g) → 2ZnO(s) + 2SO2(g) + energy
questions.text: Is the reaction above EXOTHERMIC or ENDOTHERMIC? Give a reason for the answer.

questions.context: Oxygen gas consists of oxygen molecules.
questions.text: Define the term molecule.
questions.memo_answer: A group of two or more atoms that are covalently bonded and that functions as a unit.

questions.text: Draw the Lewis dot diagram of the oxygen molecule (O2).
questions.memo_answer: O=O: the two O atoms share two electron pairs (a double bond); each O atom has two lone pairs.

questions.context: During the reaction above, 7 g ZnS reacts completely with oxygen gas. Calculate the:
questions.text: Number of moles of ZnS that has reacted
questions.topic: Quantitative aspects: stoichiometry and gas volume

questions.text: Mass O2 needed
questions.topic: Quantitative aspects: stoichiometry and gas volume
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 6.1.4.)
n(O2) = 3/2 n(ZnS) = 3/2 (0,072) = 0,108 mol
n = m / M: 0,108 = m / 32
m = 3,46 g

questions.text: Volume of SO2(g) produced at STP
questions.topic: Quantitative aspects: stoichiometry and gas volume
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 6.1.4.)
n(SO2) = n(ZnS) = 0,072 mol
n = V / Vm: 0,072 = V / 22,4
V(SO2) = 1,62 dm³

questions.context: 6.2 Consider the incomplete equation for the chemical reaction below. Zn(s) + H2SO4(aq) → X + H2(g)
questions.text: Write down the NAME of the acid in the equation above.

questions.text: Write down the FORMULA of product X.

questions.text: Name the type of reaction illustrated above. Choose from ACID- BASE REACTION, PRECIPITATION REACTION or REDOX REACTION. Explain the answer.

Redox (reaction)

questions.text: Briefly describe a test that can be used to verify the formation of hydrogen gas during the reaction above.

questions.context: (Start on a new page.) | 7.1 The relationship between conductivity and the concentration of ions in two electrolytes, NaCℓ(aq) and CaCℓ2(aq), of the SAME concentration are investigated.
questions.text: Define the term electrolyte.
questions.memo_answer: An electrolyte is a solution that conducts electricity through the movement of ions.

questions.text: Is the water molecule POLAR or NON-POLAR? Give a reason for the answer.
questions.memo_answer:
Polar
It has two oppositely charged poles.

questions.text: For this investigation, write down the: (a) Independent variable (1) (b) Dependent variable (1)

questions.context: The NaCℓ(aq) is added dropwise to distilled water in a beaker and the conductivity of the solution is measured after the addition of each drop. The experiment is repeated for the CaCℓ2(aq). The results obtained are shown in the table below. [NUMBER OF DROPS 0-7. Conductivity of NaCℓ(aq) (mA): 0,18; 0,34; 0,55; 0,74; 0,92; 1,10; 1,29; 1,47. Conductivity of CaCℓ2(aq) (mA): 0,18; 0,55; 0,91; 1,29; 1,47; 1,84; 2,21; 2,21.]
questions.text: Write down a balanced equation for the dissociation of NaCℓ(s) in water.
questions.memo_answer:
NaCℓ(s) → Na⁺(aq) + Cℓ⁻(aq) (over H2O(ℓ)); balanced
NOTE: ignore phases.

questions.text: Which electrolyte, NaCℓ(aq) or CaCℓ2(aq), has the higher conductivity? Give a reason for the answer.
questions.memo_answer:
CaCℓ2
A higher concentration of ions forms in solution.

questions.context: 7.2 A learner is supplied with two unlabelled bottles containing potassium salts. She knows that one bottle contains a SULPHATE and the other a CARBONATE. To distinguish between the two salts she adds a few drops of barium nitrate, Ba(NO3)2(aq), to a solution of each salt in two separate test tubes, A and B, as shown below. [Test tube A: white precipitate that dissolves in nitric acid; test tube B: white precipitate insoluble in nitric acid.] The learner finds that a white precipitate forms in each test tube. After the addition of nitric acid, the precipitate in test tube A dissolves to release a gas, while the precipitate in test tube B remains. Write down the:
questions.text: FORMULA of the POTASSIUM SALT in test tube A
FORMULA of the precipitate that forms in test tube B
Balanced equation for the reaction that explains why the precipitate dissolves in test tube A after the addition of nitric acid
questions.memo_answer:
BaCO3(s) + 2HNO3(aq) → Ba(NO3)2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(ℓ); balanced
NOTE: ignore phases.

questions.context: QUESTION 8 (Start on a new page.) The simplified diagram below represents the water cycle. Condensation and evaporation are two of the processes in the water cycle. [Diagram: process A from the dam up to water vapour; process B from water vapour to clouds; process C from clouds down to the ground; process D from the ground to underground water.] 8.1 Define the term:
questions.text: Condensation
questions.memo_answer: Condensation is the process during which a gas or vapour changes to a liquid.

questions.text: Evaporation
questions.memo_answer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into a vapour at any temperature below the boiling point.

questions.context: 8.2 Write down the name of:
questions.text: Process A
Process B
Process C
Process D
Describe the term hydrosphere with reference to the different phases present.
questions.memo_answer: The hydrosphere is the water of the Earth. It is found as liquid water, ice and water vapour in the atmosphere.
